name: Dry platelet pack
subtitle: clotting cells stored dry on a shelf

effects.effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out

effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out
how: Platelets stop bleeding, and bleeding is what kills most people who could otherwise have been saved after a crash or in childbirth. They last five days, must be kept rocking at room temperature, and so exist only in big hospitals. Loading platelets with the glass-forming proteins that let tardigrades dry out would let them be freeze-dried into a sachet that sits in an ambulance for a year and is mixed with water at the roadside.
obstacle: Getting the proteins inside a cell that has no nucleus, and proving the rehydrated platelets still clot rather than clump at once.
why: Sugar-dried platelets work partly; glass proteins might close the gap, untried at scale.
real: Tardigrade CAHS D plus trehalose has been shown (DARPA-funded, Sci Rep 2023) to stabilise dried human Factor VIII, and freeze-dried/trehalose-loaded platelets exist separately, but no work was found applying tardigrade glass-forming proteins to platelets for transfusion.
